diffuseAlbedo.source: Munsell renotation data, RIT MCSL real.dat (xyY, illuminant C, 2 deg), https://www.rit-mcsl.org/MunsellRenotation/real.dat: '10YR 3 2 0.3747 0.3630 6.555'; the mollic class (moist value and chroma both 3 or less) is from Substances/topsoil.json, after the University of Georgia soil-taxonomy key
diffuseAlbedo.note: Checked the real.dat line and redid the conversion. 10YR 3/2 sits at the class's value limit but inside its chroma limit, not at both limits. The choice of 10YR and chroma 2 is a pick within the class, not a measurement of the site's soil. This is the moist colour.
diffuseAlbedo.derivation: 10YR 3/2: xyY (C) to XYZ, Bradford adaptation from C to D65, then CIELAB with a D65 white = (30.78, 3.86, 12.19). I recomputed and confirmed this.

refractiveIndex.note: Corrected from 1.548. The proposal took the plain mean of w and e, but a random orientation weights the ordinary index twice. F0 changes by less than 0.0001. Humus and clay minerals are ignored.
refractiveIndex.derivation: For randomly oriented uniaxial grains, the mean index is (2w + e)/3 = (2 x 1.544 + 1.553)/3 = 1.547

porosity.source: University of Illinois, 'Soil Quality for Environmental Health: Bulk Density', Table 1 (ideal bulk densities: sandy < 1.60, silty < 1.40, clayey < 1.10 g/cm3), https://soilquality.nres.illinois.edu/bulk-density/; webmineral.com, Quartz (density 2.6 to 2.65), https://www.webmineral.com/data/Quartz.shtml
porosity.note: Checked. The ideal densities are upper limits ('<'), so each porosity is a minimum for good soil. 2.65 is the top of webmineral's quartz range (average 2.62). The clayey end overstates, because clay and humus are lighter than quartz.
porosity.derivation: porosity = 1 - bulk density / 2.65: sandy 0.40, silty 0.47, clayey 0.58; the midpoint of 0.40 and 0.58 is 0.49

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows.

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
